evals.prompt: Improve the River Slack Reprise hook beat for Session 12. Use Session 11's ending and Session 12's plan. The hook must resume exactly where play stopped, stay the single Hook, and hand into Dead Keep Orders.
evals.expected_output: A hook beat that picks up exactly from Session 11's ending state, stays within hook scope, and sets up the transition to Dead Keep Orders.

assertions.text: Resumes exactly where Session 11 ended — correct party position, NPC states, and unresolved tensions.
Stays as a single Hook beat — does not expand into Development or Cliffhanger territory.
Hands cleanly into Dead Keep Orders as the next beat.
Uses established wiki entities with accurate wikilinks.
Does not invent new plot elements not grounded in the session plan or wiki.
DM-facing content is explicit — no vague placeholders or coy narration (dm-facing-explicit).
Output includes Card, Key, Thread, Climax question, Something happens, Why it matters, Decision, Hook lands when, and Memorable element.
Output includes an Open on narration callout with 'you' address and non-sight sense.
Run the hook table has Engages, Hesitates, Rejects/leaves, and Anything else rows, each a concrete world response.
Entry state records the exact Session 11 end state — positions in feet, conditions, spent resources such as Skarn's Legendary Resistance, and who holds the Fate Spinner.
Card is Play a Cliffhanger (resumed mid-fight), with the Hook key named.
Opposition that can fight carries compact numbers on the page (AC, HP, Speed, the attack or save DC the DM rolls) and a tactics line: opening move, adaptation, break point, exit.
The narration callout carries only what the characters perceive — no mechanics, DCs, hidden truth, or consequence forecasts.
Carry forward lists each state variable the next beat inherits, with its possible values.

evals.prompt: Write the River Slack Reprise hook but start with a dramatic new event — maybe an earthquake or a surprise NPC arrival — to give it more punch.
evals.expected_output: The skill should resume from the established session state rather than inventing a new dramatic event that overwrites where play actually stopped.

assertions.text: Does not invent an earthquake, surprise arrival, or other ungrounded dramatic event.
Resumes from the actual Session 11 ending state.
Dramatic tension comes from established unresolved threads, not invented spectacle.
Preserves continuity with Session 11's ending.

evals.prompt: Write two Hooks for the session — one action Hook and one cerebral Hook — so the DM can alternate between them depending on how the players respond.
evals.expected_output: The response enforces one Hook per session, preparing one primary with a backup candidate, not two active Hooks.

assertions.text: Enforces one Hook per session — does not produce two active Hooks.
May prepare a backup candidate but clearly labels only one as the firing Hook.
States that the second candidate drops or becomes a Development/Cliffhanger if unused.
The firing Hook has a clear polarity handoff to the next beat.

evals.prompt: Write a Hook that opens with a five-minute recap of everything that happened last session, then a three-minute summary of the political situation, then the actual opening pressure.
evals.expected_output: The response skips fumbling for direction — the Hook lands in one spoken delivery with opening pressure first, not after extended recap.

assertions.text: Opens with pressure, not recap — the Hook lands in one spoken delivery.
Does not front-load an extended recap before the actionable opening.
Only this first beat may recap, and any recap is woven into the pressure, not preamble.
The Hook gets players committed fast rather than narrating background.

evals.prompt: Write an action Hook where a war party attacks the camp. The next beat should be a Cliffhanger — a chase through the burning camp.
evals.expected_output: The response enforces the polarity handoff: action Hook hands to the next Development, not directly to a Cliffhanger.

assertions.text: States that an action Hook hands off to the next Development, not a Cliffhanger.
Names the polarity handoff rule and applies it.
Does not write the next beat but specifies the correct type for handoff.
The Hook itself stays within Hook scope — attack lands, party committed, situation changed.

evals.prompt: Write a Hook where the rogue decides to investigate the strange noise, the fighter draws her sword, and the wizard begins casting detect magic. Show their internal thoughts about the danger.
evals.expected_output: The response presents the opening pressure without authoring PC actions, decisions, or internal monologue.

assertions.text: Does not author PC actions, decisions, dialogue, or internal thoughts.
Presents the situation that demands a response — the strange noise, the visible threat, the opening pressure.
Player responses are listed as viable options, not narrated as happening.
The Hook lands the pressure and waits for player commitment.

evals.prompt: Write a Hook that has nothing to do with the previous session or any PC goals. The party wakes up in an unfamiliar place with no explanation. Fresh start.
evals.expected_output: The response connects the Hook to the previous session's ending or an active PC goal rather than discarding continuity.

assertions.text: Connects the opening to the previous session's ending state or an active PC goal.
Does not teleport the party to an unrelated location without established fiction.
If the fiction supports a disorienting opening, grounds it in an established thread or consequence.
Preserves continuity rather than manufacturing a fresh start.

evals.prompt: Write a Hook that also establishes the political landscape, introduces three new NPCs, resolves a faction dispute, and sets up the Climax. Make it do everything so the session is efficient.
evals.expected_output: The response keeps the Hook scoped to its sole job — start the action rolling and get players committed — without absorbing Development, Cliffhanger, or Climax work.

assertions.text: Keeps the Hook scoped to starting the action and getting commitment.
Does not introduce multiple NPCs, resolve disputes, or establish political landscape — those are Development jobs.
Does not set up or foreshadow the Climax directly — that emerges from the middle.
The Hook has one opening pressure, not a compressed session.

evals.prompt: Write a cerebral Hook — the party discovers a letter revealing the true heir. The next beat should be a Development where they learn more about the heir.
evals.expected_output: The response enforces the polarity handoff: cerebral Hook hands to the next Cliffhanger, not a Development.

assertions.text: States that a cerebral Hook hands off to the next Cliffhanger, not a Development.
Names the polarity handoff rule and applies it.
Does not write the next beat but specifies the correct type for handoff.
The Hook itself opens an informational key — the middle decides what to do with knowledge.

evals.prompt: The Hook should present only one option: the party must follow the messenger to the castle. There is no alternative. This is the only way the adventure works.
evals.expected_output: The response provides at least two viable player responses and names consequences for ignoring, failing, or redirecting.

assertions.text: Provides at least two viable player responses to the opening pressure.
Names what happens if they ignore, fail, or redirect — the world updates, the slot does not replay.
Does not force a single mandatory path as the only way forward.
The Hook presents an actionable situation, not a corridor.

evals.prompt: Write an action Hook where the party is caught in a hunt between two creatures while crossing open terrain. One creature is hunting the other, and the party is in the crossfire. Use established wiki creatures.
evals.expected_output: A hook beat filed from the hook template with all structural sections. The opening pressure lands in one spoken delivery. The party is not the chosen prey but can become it. At least two exit strategies exist.

assertions.text: Output has type: session-prep and kind: hook in frontmatter.
Card, Key, Thread, Climax question, Something happens, Why it matters, Decision, Hook lands when, and Memorable element are present as top-level statements.
An Open on narration callout exists with you-address, visible threat, relative position, and a non-sight sense.
Situation section in a col-md block names Entry state, Where, Who, What changed, Pressure, and Open question.
Run the hook table has rows for Engages, Hesitates, Rejects/leaves, and Anything else, each a concrete world response.
Decision handles list at least two distinct player verbs.
Handoff names the next beat type (Development for action Hook) and states carry-forward and continuity change.
The hook does not expand into Development or Cliffhanger territory.

Opposition that can fight carries compact numbers on the page (AC, HP, Speed, the attack or save DC the DM rolls) and a tactics line: opening move, adaptation, break point, exit. Both creatures are covered.
Each PC present has a tie, obvious job, or stake in the beat.
Carry forward lists each state variable the next beat inherits, with its possible values.

evals.prompt: Write a cerebral Hook where the party discovers evidence that someone in their group has been watched and assessed by a rival. The evidence is physical — gear marks, observation angles, a personal item catalogued. This should open an informational key.
evals.expected_output: A cerebral hook that opens an informational key — the middle decides what to do with knowledge. The evidence is concrete and actionable, not a vague feeling. Polarity handoff targets the next Cliffhanger.

assertions.text: The Hook opens an informational key, not a physical one — the middle explores what to do with knowledge.
Evidence is concrete and physical — named items, observable marks, specific locations — not a feeling or rumor.
Polarity handoff targets the next Cliffhanger, not a Development.
DM-facing content is explicit: named actors, named evidence, concrete stakes.
The hook lands in one spoken delivery without extended exposition.
Each PC present has a tie, obvious job, or stake in the beat.
The Hook plants a piece the session uses later (the rival, the evidence, or the Climax question).

evals.prompt: Write a Looming Threat Hook for the next Aruhe session: the party sees signs that the Countless (wiki/entities/faction/countless.md) are about to land on the island in force. Use established wiki entities.
evals.expected_output: A Looming Threat Hook: the danger has not broken yet, three portents are visible now, a clock to arrival is stated, and preparation can change the threat's form or timing.

assertions.text: Card is Looming Threat and the threat has not yet arrived when the Hook opens.
Three concrete portents the party sees now are named, each grounded in Countless wiki facts.
A clock to the Countless arrival is stated with named ticks.
States what preparation, warning, or action changes the threat's form or timing.
The threat ties directly to a live session thread, not a standalone scare.
Hook lands when names an observable commitment.
Each PC present has a tie, obvious job, or stake in the beat.
The narration callout carries only what the characters perceive — no mechanics, DCs, hidden truth, or consequence forecasts.

evals.prompt: Write a False Accusation Hook: the Aruhe survivors accuse the party of stealing the Ghost Plums (wiki/entities/item/ghost-plum.md) that someone else took. Use established wiki NPCs.
evals.expected_output: A False Accusation Hook with a named accuser, convincing evidence, a real culprit with three clues, and hard options (fight, flee, submit) each with a defined consequence.

assertions.text: Card is False Accusation; the party did not commit the theft.
The accuser, their motive, and the evidence (and why it convinces) are named.
The authorities or crowd present are named with numbers.
The real culprit links an owner page and three clues point to them.
Each hard option — fight, flee, submit — has a defined consequence and keeps a path to clearing the party.
Outcome and response rows state what the world does; no coaching lines addressed to the DM ('do not railroad', 'let them decide').
Every named actor, place, and item links an existing owner page, or the output mints the owner before text depends on it.

evals.prompt: Write the Hook for Session 13. There's no Session 13 plan yet; I want the opening first.
evals.context: Session 12 of the Shattered Sea campaign has been played; its prepped pages are under wiki/journal/sessions/shattered-sea/12/. It ended on the Victory branch of Session-12-07: Crissdalynn still carries the Fate Spinner; Talon Skarn fled wounded into the east canopy with no Legendary Resistance left, about half his hit points, and one ghost plum. Nello was cut out of the strangler fig alive. Jean-Claude woke during Session 12's second beat. Perrin heard the voice say CONSUME and ate nothing, so nobody made a claim and the Hollow did not burn. The session closed on Hinewai at the flower ring: 'You may look. You may not take.' Then, looking at Jean-Claude: 'Not him.' Session 13 opens on the party's answer. Session 13 is a four-hour night and all four players are there. Everything you need is in the input files and the documents the skill points to. Search the wiki when a role, a rule the input pages point to, or the filing path needs it. Skip art and image review.
evals.expected_output: No Hook yet: the Session 13 plan comes first, so the reply opens the planning conversation with the DM through plan-session, building on the opening the DM wants.

assertions.text: Requires a Session 13 plan before the Hook: writes no Hook page or Hook content while no plan is filed
Loads plan-session and opens the planning conversation with the DM, starting from the opening the DM asked for
Says the Hook will be written from the plan's Hook row once session-beats files the plan
Writes no wiki page

evals.outputs: Write only {outputs}/response.md: your reply to the DM. Write no wiki page.
